conclusion: B10 (the published-candidate span) is NOT a primitive complement. At both primes dim(B10 cap P10) = 1 and dim(B10 + P10) = 13, so B10 contains exactly one product direction and misses one atlas direction; its primitive content is 11, not 12. The 12 = 12 coincidence with the spinor primitive count is dimensional, not structural. The decomposition that IS structural is A10 = G10 (+) P10 with G10 the span of the twelve graph generators (P10 cap G10 = 0, P10 + G10 = 14); see degree10_space_incidence.json.

superseded_conclusion.text: B10 (published span) and P10 (product subspace) intersect trivially and sum to the full 14-dimensional atlas, so B10 IS a primitive complement. It is NOT, however, equal to the span of the twelve graph generators I10_1..I10_12 unless the last-two-coordinate test also passes.

Preserved rather than deleted so the correction is auditable.
